newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Dec 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Dec 12.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- KIER WINDFALL NETS 47,000 POUNDS EACH FOR STAFF

Staff at construction group Kier will receive share windfalls of an average 47,000 pounds stg each when the company begins trading on the Stock Exchange today. Around 900 building foremen, site managers and office staff invested an average of 4,500 pounds stg each in a buyout of the company in 1992 from Hanson. The shares originally bought at 10p will start trading at 170p.
-- CREST GIVES FEE REBATE AFTER OPERATION DELAYS

The computerised share settlement scheme, Crest, is to payback half of its peak-time user costs. The board agreed yesterday, to reduce the 60 pence stg standard fee for sending information to the computer to 30 pence stg for the past two months due to problems and delays encountered by users over recent weeks. The rebate will cost Crest in the region of 111,000 pounds stg.
-- COST OF BT CALLS TO ORANGE SET FOR NEAR-DOUBLE RISE

From February next year, the cost of British Telecom calls to Orange and One 2 One mobile phones will nearly double. The reason for the increase is that Orange and One 2 One hope to get a bigger proportion of revenue from BT for the calls that end up on their network. At the present neither operator is charging BT the full cost of carrying these telephone calls, and an increase will be passed on to BT customers.
THE TIMES
-- SHELL TO INVEST 10 BILLION DOLLARS IN MEXICAN GULF

Shell Oil has plans to invest as much as 10 billion dollars US in deep water oil production in the Gulf of Mexico over the next four years. THe US subsidiary of the Anglo-Dutch oil company is the largest leaseholder in water depth beyond 15,000 feet in the Gulf of Mexico, and has eight or more undisclosed projects in preparation, with the aim of achieving a quick build-up in oil production over the four-year period.
-- HERON HERALDS 1 BILLION POUNDS INVESTMENT

Heron, the property group, is to buy office buildings in central London and to develop a chain of multiplex cinemas in Spain. The group could spend up to 1 billion pounds stg as part of a massive investment in property. The first deal to be announced in the new year will be the purchase of a landmark commercial building in London, followed by a joint venture to develop the cinema complexes in Spain.
-- WALL STREET DIVES BUT BASE RATE PROTECTS LONDON

The jitters struck Wall Street again yesterday, and other markets were pulled down in its wake. The loss of confidence was prompted by partly by fears that Japanese investors may become less enthusiastic buyers of US assets. The nervous atmosphere was present in the London market but losses were not dramatic, finishing the day 53.2 points lower.
THE GUARDIAN
-- LEVITT FACES COMPANIES ACT CHARGE

Former life assurance company director Roger Levitt is being prosecuted for allegedly breaking the seven-year ban on his acting as a director imposed in 1990, according to The Guardian. He is charged with being a 'shadow director' in a boxing management company by the Department of Trade and Industry.
-- NEW ANTI-SMOKING DRUGS WILL AID FIGHT TO KICK HABIT

Glaxo Wellcome and Pharmacia & Upjohn will today find out if the US Food and Drug Administration have approved their new anti-smoking products, a tablet from Glaxo and an inhaler from Pharmacia. Other drug companies are making plans to target the market of smokers keen to quit.
-- LIFE POLICIES STILL MIS-SOLD

The Personal Investment Authority has for the first time disclosed the lapse records of individual insurance companies, based on how soon policies are cashed in after purchase. The record shows one in four mortgage endowments sold by some companies are surrendered within the first two years, despite the prospect of heavy penalties. This indicates the unsuitability of many policies, the watchdog says.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- BRITAIN 'LAGGING IN INVESTMENT'

A new report from the Machine Tool Technologies Association and Oxford Economic Forecasting has challenged government claims that British industry compares well with other industrial economies. The report presents figures that show the share of investment in GDP is lower than elsewhere, as is spending on research and development.
-- MINISTERS MOVE TO SCRAP HI-TECH PRODUCT TARIFFS

The USA, Japan and the European Union yesterday made progress towards removing tariffs on information technology products, with an agreement in principle made at a meeting of ministers of the World Trade Organisation in Singapore. Other nations were also asked to join in opening up the industry, worth 363 billion pounds stg in annual sales.
